verdicts.justification: Repro output matched the claim exactly: 'alpha=0.2 scatter0: n=150 non-nan=1 / scatter1: n=150 non-nan=0' and identical at alpha=0.6 -- 299 of 300 points NaN'd out of the plotly scatter traces regardless of alpha. Code confirms this is deliberate (plotly_backend.py:520-529 NaNs points 'enclosed' by the hull because the Mesh3d is 'always rendered fully opaque (opacity=1.0)' with alpha baked into the base color, _mesh3d_trace docstring line ~1228), but the plot() docstring contradicts it: alpha is documented as 'surface opacity' and line 1028 describes 'plotly's translucent Mesh3d', and keep_points defaults True. Evidence PNGs verified: pl8_plotly_surface_alpha02_points_gone.png shows two opaque pastel hulls with ZERO visible points; pl8_mpl_surface_alpha02_comparison.png shows all points through genuinely translucent mpl hulls for identical arguments. Documented feature (translucency + kept points) does not exist in the plotly backend -- major.

Repro reproduced verbatim: 'warnings: []' and density-on artists identical to a no-density baseline (6x Line3DCollection cube edges only -- nothing drawn) for 80 points with a constant zero z-column. Control in the same run: all-identical points DO warn ('density: dataset 0 is degenerate (...singular data covariance matrix...); skipping its density.'), proving the warning path exists but the coplanar case bypasses it (pipeline rescaling leaves std ~1e-16, gaussian_kde fits, grid density evaluates to 0, zero iso meshes, no warning). plot.py:1113-1116 explicitly promises: degenerate '(singular covariance -- e.g. exactly duplicated/collinear/coplanar points) has its density silently skipped with a UserWarning'. Promise broken for exactly the coplanar case it names. Evidence e16b (2D collinear delta-ridge) visually consistent.

Docs-only inaccuracy: doc.
